CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow up of chronic problems.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Anna is a 44-year-old female with a past medical history significant for arthritis, gout, and reflux who presents for follow up of her chronic problems. It has been approximately six months since last visit.

Arthritis: Patient reports her arthritis is starting to get better. She has been doing pilates and lifting weights which has helped build up muscle and the joint pain has been going away. She completed physical therapy for her right knee with good results and has built up her strength. She is now walking approximately one to one and a half miles per day.

Gout: Patient had an episode of gout affecting her right first toe approximately two months ago. The medication helped resolve it. She is taking allopurinol as prescribed with no issues and denies any further flare-ups.

Reflux: Patient was placed on omeprazole and instructed to make dietary modifications. She has made some dietary modifications but has not completely eliminated stone yet. She continues to have some episodes and reports throwing up in the mornings with actual vomiting. She also endorses abdominal pain and bloating. Last bowel movement was two days ago and was normal with no blood. Denies weight loss, fever, or chills.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for nausea, vomiting, abdominal distension, and abdominal pain. Denies diarrhea, weight loss, fever, or chills. No blood in stool.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs are within normal limits. Heart sounds good. Lungs sound good. Abdominal exam shows pain to right upper quadrant on palpation with no rebound or guarding and no peritoneal signs. Right knee shows slight effusion with some pain to palpation and decreased range of motion.

RESULTS
Autoimmune panel: All within normal limits.
Right knee X-ray: No fracture. Shows residual arthritis.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Reflux with nausea and vomiting: Continue omeprazole 40 milligrams once daily. Continue dietary modifications. Obtain right upper quadrant ultrasound to rule out gallstones. Check labs.

2. Gout: Continue allopurinol 100 milligrams once daily. Refill ordered.

3. Arthritis of right knee: Very pleased with current progress. Continue pilates and continue using the knee. Follow up regarding any issues and discuss further imaging or intervention as needed.
